summary: Machine-checkable editorial rules extracted from doc_architecture.md section 4.

rules.summary: Chapter- and part-level reader guidance belongs at the opening before operative sections; local guidance may appear adjacent to the material it explains.

rules.legacy_ref: doc_architecture file-top stack and section-opening widgets
rules.summary:
File-top and section-opening widget stack: placement → reader guidance → Trace → D/A/C contiguous (blank lines only; no
/owner/prose between); owner line and operative prose follow the stack.
Trace blocks are blue collapsible details, collapsed by default.
Trace placement under owning unit; Chapter Six default owner is subarticle.
Trace contents: Upstream, Downstream, Read with inside block; no Definitions line.
D/A/C widget scope, trigger, roadmap exclusion, row shape, annotation prose, spacer discipline.
With Trace: D/A/C or inline Definition immediately after Trace. Without Trace: D/A/C is first block under heading.
Collapsible D/A/C keeps trailing br; inline Definition line does not.
Chapter One D/A/C widgets preserve functional row order.
Single collapsed Corpus placement widget at file top; no visible binding banner, Application baseline, or redundant file-top prose.
Chapter Three section 1 link-only A-Z in-chapter index.
In-paragraph operative links only when load-bearing and sparse.
Chapter Five definitions exclude institutional machinery and rights gloss density.
Chapter Five editorial order, separators, compound heading alignment.
One --- between definition units (above <a id> anchors); no stacked or wrong-side rules; no redundant (Constitutional) suffix.
One visible Chapter Five definition label per term.
Lexical substitutions, forum/court vocabulary, capitalization drift.
Advisory jargon phrase scan from lexical_guardrails.json.
Chapter Six #### subarticles with operative bullets need In plain terms line.
Chapter Six ### article intros use *Article neighbors:* for visible coordination prose after aims/tetrad blocks.
Heuristic O/E/C-shaped gloss blocks outside Chapter Five owners.
Companion family cites link the authoritative subfile, not the layer wrapper; CJS-3.n is the public cluster ID.
Chapter Six article titles and Roman numerals from part files.
Layer stack, orthogonal tags, placement rules; generated definition_hierarchy index.
Definition-anchored primary/secondary/tertiary measurement tiers inform E and C authoring; O stays ontological.
Seed ↔ hierarchy ch00_measurement sync and bidirectional Ch00 §3 owner links.
Cross-implementation topic routing via CJS-0.1.

rules.legacy_ref: binding corpus must not depend on doc_architecture for meaning or routing
rules.summary: Binding corpus may cite doc_architecture only when classifying it as non-binding/support or as a reading-chain footer terminus.

rules.legacy_ref: Chapter Four ↔ Chapter Seven pointer discipline
rules.summary: Chapter Seven must cite Chapters Two through Four when applying verification-substrate rules; must not restate Chapter Four §§1–6.

rules.legacy_ref: companion numeric prefixes are chapter labels
rules.summary: Numbered cjs_/cs_/ci_/cf_ files share a numeric prefix only as same-chapter parts; family 01 is the unique scope page.
One current fragment id per heading. When a section is dropped or renumbered, retarget live citations and delete the old id; do not keep fossil or legacy redirect anchors.

rules.legacy_ref: section-label cite vs current heading number
rules.summary: Markdown links whose visible text contains §N (or is only a dotted number such as 4.1) must resolve to a heading numbered N or a dotted parent/child of N; the fragment must exist. Range-start cites such as §§ 1–12 are allowed when they target the range start. Named fragments without a numeric id prefix are not compared to the § label. implementation/ and evaluation/ sources are out of scope.
When a §N cite is dotted-related to the target heading, that heading must carry a current-numbering fragment id (compact prefix 54- or hyphenated 5-4-).
Numbered ATX headings in core_*.md grouped by parent prefix and heading level must not duplicate a sibling number; last components must be consecutive integers. A file need not start at §1.
